title: How Does Your Nose Smell Things? 👃 Fun Facts for Kids
description:
Smells are made of tiny floating bits! Leo asks, big sister Mia explains how your nose and brain work together to smell, in under a minute.

The CurioKids Club: short, curious answers to kids' big questions. Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/@CurioKidsClub

lines.text: Mia, how does my nose smell things?
Everything that smells gives off teeny tiny bits called molecules. They float through the air, way too small to see!
So when I smell cookies, little cookie bits are in my nose?
Yep! When you breathe in, those bits zoom up your nose to a special patch, high up inside.
That patch has lots of smell cells. Different cells catch different smells, a bit like keys fitting into locks.
The smell cells send a message to your brain, and your brain works it out and says, 'Mmm, cookies!'
Why do I sniff when I want to smell something better?
Sniffing pulls in more air, so more smell bits reach the smell patch. Big sniff, big smell!
Does my nose help me taste, too?
It sure does! Smell and taste work as a team. That's why food can taste plain when you have a stuffy nose.
Tiny smell bits, smell cells and my brain. Noses are awesome!
They sure are! Ask a grown-up to subscribe to The Curio Kids Club for more wonders! And next time someone asks... how does your nose smell things?
